newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed over 1.5 percent lower on Tuesday due to weaker bonds and a lower dollar. Dealers said stocks were likely to fall further.
The AEX share index, falling 11.67 points to 741.73, could slip to 729 points, dealers said. This level is seen as the next support level after the index fell below 750 points today.
Dealers said the current correction was only the other side of the recent rally since the index was well below 700 points at the start of 1997.
Only 58 issues on the Amsterdam exchange advanced today, while 252 issues declined.
"The rally was mainly dollar-driven", said one dealer, adding a fall of the dollar was hurting the Dutch stock market.
Financials were the sector hit most by the lower dollar and weaker bond market.
Bank-insurer ING dipped 2.40 guilders to 73.70 and ABN AMRO Bank ended 3.20 guilders lower at 130.00.
Insurer Aegon fell 4.00 guilders to 134.80, but dealers said the stock was not likely to fall much further as the firm was expected to announce strong 1996 results on Friday.
Analysts forecast a rise in net profits of over 17 percent to 1.55 billion guilders for Aegon.
Builders were seen as a safe haven as long as the downward pressure on the share market continues. Builder Volker Stevin rose strongly despite the downtrend in the market today.
Volker Stevin, which announced last week it was planning to merge with sector rival Kondor Wessels and also posted strong 1996-results, rose 4.00 guilders to close at 211.50.
Volker Stevin touched an all time high at 214.00 guilders per share earlier during today's session.
Builder BAM also showed a strong performance, rising 6.50 guilders to 125, surpassing an earlier high of 124.00 guilders.
"Looking at price-earnings it is an interesting stock."

Shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland slipped 0.30 guilders to 99.30, but dealers said they saw some upward potential for the stock as IHC was trading well under its high of 115.80 guilders per share, dating from January 24.
Publisher VNU slipped 0.10 guilders to 40.80, after posting a rise in net profits and an upbeat forecast for 1997.
"VNU is a growth stock, but the expected growth in net profits for 1997 is already priced in," said one dealer.
Post and telecoms group KPN and steel and aluminium group Hoogovens were among the few gainers in Amsterdam.
